'''Klaus Kalb''' (born 1942) is a German [[lichenologist]] and an authority on tropical [[lichen]]s. Born in [[Nuremberg]], he studied at the [[University of Erlangen–Nuremberg]] before pursuing a career that significantly advanced the field of lichenology, particularly in Brazil. Kalb's work in [[São Paulo]] from 1978 to 1981 led to a collaboration with Brazilian lichenologist Marcelo Pinto Marcelli, which is considered a model for non-commercial benefit-sharing in taxonomic research. He later became an associate professor at the [[University of Regensburg]] and is known for editing the [[exsiccata]] series ''Lichenes Neotropici''. Kalb's contributions to lichenology include over 120 scientific publications, the [[species description|description]] of numerous new species, and the development of a substantial lichen collection. His work has been recognised through various honours, including four lichen genera and numerous species named after him, as well as a [[Festschrift]] published in 2007 to mark his retirement.

==Biography==
[[File:Vainionora americana 456701.jpg|thumb|right|''[[Vainionora americana]]'' was described as a new species by Kalb and colleagues in 2004.<ref name="Kalb 2004"/>]]

Klaus Kalb was born in [[Nuremberg]] in 1942 and grew up in southern [[Bavaria]]. From 1960 to 1965 he studied biology, chemistry, and geography at the [[University of Erlangen–Nuremberg]]. Kalb was greatly interested in lichens and decided to pursue a [[doctoral degree]]; his thesis work was about lichen communities in the [[Ötztal Alps]].<ref name="Kärnefelt 2012"/>

From 1978 to 1981, Kalb was a teacher at the [[Colégio Visconde de Porto Seguro]] in [[São Paulo, Brazil]].<ref name="Hertel et al. 2017"/> This position afforded him the opportunity to initiate research into tropical lichens. During this period, Kalb made significant contributions to the field of lichenology in Brazil through his collaboration with Brazilian lichenologist Marcelo Pinto Marcelli. Kalb provided three years of intensive training to Marcelli and later assisted him in completing his PhD thesis in 1987. This collaboration is considered an outstanding example of non-commercial benefit-sharing in taxonomic research, laying the foundation for modern lichenology in Brazil.<ref name="Lücking 2020"/>

Kalb earned his [[habilitation]] from the [[University of Regensburg]] in 1989, becoming an associate professor with that institution.<ref name="Kärnefelt 2012"/> He is editing the [[exsiccata]] series ''Lichenes Neotropici'',<ref>{{cite web |title=Lichenes Neotropici: IndExs ExsiccataID=220498562 |website=IndExs – Index of Exsiccatae |publisher=Botanische Staatssammlung München |url=https://www.botanischestaatssammlung.de/DatabaseClients/IndExs/Exsiccatae_IndExs_Details.jsp?ExsiccataID=220498562 |access-date=24 May 2024}}</ref> starting with 2017 together with [[André Aptroot]].

Kalb's approach to collaboration and mentorship has been praised for embodying the spirit of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and the Nagoya Protocol, more than a decade before the CBD was established. His work with Brazilian lichenologists has led to the training of multiple generations of researchers in the field.<ref name="Lücking 2020"/>

In 2014, the [[University of Wisconsin]] herbarium purchased Kalb's lichen collection of 60,000 specimens for $75,000. With the acquisition of Kalb's collection, rich in tropical and European specimens, the [[herbarium]] houses about 70% of the world's known lichen [[taxon|taxa]].<ref name="Jones 2014"/>

==Recognition==

In 2007, on the occasion of his retirement, Kalb was honoured with a [[Festschrift]],<ref name="Frisch et al. 2008"/> featuring 24 scientific papers written by 51 authors. The Festschrift included a publication list, a list of [[taxon|taxa]] described by him and of taxa named after him.<ref name="Printzen 2008"/>

===Eponyms===

Four lichen genera have been named in honour of Kalb:<ref name="Hertel et al. 2017"/> ''[[Kalbiana]]'' {{small|Henssen (1988)}}; ''[[Kalbographa]]'' {{small|Lücking (2007)}}; ''[[Kalbionora]]'' {{small|Sodamuk, S.D.Leav. & Lumbsch (2017)}}; and ''[[Klauskalbia]]'' {{small|S.Y.Kondr., Lőkös, E.Farkas & Hur (2021)}}.<ref name="Kondratyuk et al. 2021"/>

Many species have also been [[eponym|named to honour]] Kalb. These include:<ref name="Hertel et al. 2017"/> ''[[Acanthothecis kalbii]]'' {{small|Dal-Forno & Eliasaro (2009)}}; ''[[Acanthotrema kalbii]]'' {{small|Lücking (2012)}};  ''[[Astrochapsa kalbii]]'' {{small|Poengs., Lücking & Lumbsch (2014)}}; ''[[Byssoloma kalbii]]'' {{small|Sérus. (1996)}} ''[[Caloplaca kalbiorum]]'' {{small|S.Y.Kondr. & Kärnefelt (2007)}}; ''[[Chaenothecopsis kalbii]]'' {{small|Tibell & K.Ryman (1995)}}  ''[[Chapsa kalbii]]'' {{small|Frisch (2006)}}; ''[[Cladina kalbii]]'' {{small|Ahti (2000)}}; ''[[Coenogonium kalbii]]'' {{small|Aptroot, Lücking & L.Umaña (2006)}}; ''[[Compsocladium kalbii]]'' {{small|Frisch (2007)}}; ''[[Enterographa kalbii]]'' {{small|Sparrius (2004)}}; ''[[Gyalideopsis kalbii]]'' {{small|Vězda (1983)}}; ''[[Heterodermia kalbii]]'' {{small|M.F.N.Martins & Marcelli (2007)}};  ''[[Hypotrachyna kalbii]]'' {{small|Elix, T.H.Nash & Sipman (2009)}}; ''[[Hypotrachyna klauskalbii]]'' {{small|A.Fletcher ex Sipman, Elix & T.H.Nash (2009)}};  ''[[Lecanora kalbiana]]'' {{small|Lumbsch (1996)}}; ''[[Lecanora klauskalbii]]'' {{small|Sipman (2007)}}; ''[[Lecidea kalbii]]'' {{small|Hertel (1984)}}; ''[[Leptogium kalbii]]'' {{small|Marcelli & I.P.R.Cunha (2007)}}; ''[[Megalospora kalbii]]'' {{small|Sipman (1983)}}; ''[[Musaespora kalbii]]'' {{small|Lücking & Sérus. (1996)}}; ''[[Ocellularia kalbii]]'' {{small|Mangold, Elix & Lumbsch (2007)}}; ''[[Opegrapha blakii]]'' {{small|Ertz & Diederich (2004)}}; ''[[Opegrapha kalbii]]'' {{small|Matzer (1996)}}; ''[[Pertusaria kalbii]]'' {{small|A.W.Archer & Messuti (1998)}};  ''[[Phaeographis kalbii]]'' {{small|Staiger (2002)}}; ''[[Phyllopsora kalbii]]'' {{small|Brako (1991)}}; ''[[Physcia kalbii]]'' {{small|Moberg (1990)}}; ''[[Piccolia kalbii]]'' {{small|Van den Broeck & Ertz (2013)}}; ''[[Pseudocyphellaria kalbi]]'' {{small|D.J.Galloway (1993)}}; ''[[Pseudoparmelia kalbiana]]'' {{small|Elix & T.H.Nash (1998)}};  ''[[Rinodina kalbii]]'' {{small|Giralt & Matzer (1994)}}; ''[[Roselliniella kalbii]]'' {{small|Hafellner (1985)}}; ''[[Trichothelium kalbii]]'' {{small|Lücking (2004)}}; ''[[Usnea kalbiana]]'' {{small|A.Gerlach & P.Clerc (2017)}}; ''[[Xanthoparmelia kalbii]]'' {{small|Hale (1984)}};  ''[[Xanthoparmelia klauskalbii]]'' {{small|Elix (2007)}}; ''[[Xanthoparmelia neokalbii]]'' {{small|T.H.Nash & Elix (1995)}};<ref name="Hertel et al. 2017"/> and ''[[Lecanora kalbii]]'' {{small|Bungartz & Elix (2020)}}.<ref name="Bungartz et al. 2020"/>
